Proband-only exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous COL3A1 missense variant (c.3058G>T, p.Gly1020Cys) in exon 42, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and classified as likely pathogenic for vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

A related variant at the same codon (p.Gly1020Asp) has previously been classified as pathogenic by LOVD, supporting the mutational significance of position 1020 despite differing amino acid substitution chemistry from the patient's variant.

The patient presented with isolated cerebrovascular involvement, including fusiform aneurysmal dilation of the M1 segment of the left middle cerebral artery and diffuse tortuosity/dilation of both internal carotid arteries and the vertebrobasilar system, without extracranial vascular abnormalities on abdominal CT angiography.

Physical examination revealed minor vEDS diagnostic features including thin lips, abnormal atrophic scarring, thin skin with venous visibility, scalp alopecia, horizontal stretch marks under the arms, acrogeric appearance of hands/feet, and joint hypermobility (Beighton score 4).

The paper notes that in prior literature, glycine substitution by cysteine, serine, or aspartate destabilizes the collagen triple helix more frequently than expected, and that substitution by valine or asparagine has been associated with poorer prognosis compared to serine substitution.
The paper cites prior literature that in vEDS-associated arterial ruptures, rupture sites primarily occur in the chest and abdomen (66%), followed by the head and neck (17%), and extremities (17%).
At 1-year follow-up after diagnosis, with blood pressure management and avoidance of high-risk activities/procedures, the patient had no adverse vascular events.
A total of 56 different pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants were identified in the cohort, most commonly glycine substitutions, and 76.8% were predicted to have a dominant negative effect.
Male sex was associated with a significantly higher risk of experiencing a major vascular/GI/obstetric event compared with female sex.
Men had a significantly younger age at the time of their first major event compared with women.
Individuals with a COL3A1 glycine substitution or splice/delins/del variant had a significantly younger age at first major event compared with those with a suspected haploinsufficient variant.
When restricted to relatives only, there was no significant difference in age at first major event between the different COL3A1 variant categories, unlike in the full cohort.

Aortic dissection occurred significantly more often in individuals whose COL3A1 pathogenic variant was located in the first quarter of the collagen helical domain compared with the rest of the domain.

Having an appearance highly suggestive of vEDS (≥5 of 9 characteristic features) was not associated with a higher frequency of major events but was associated with a significantly younger age at the first major event.
Hypertension showed a trend towards association with occurrence of a major event, though not statistically significant.
Aortic aneurysms were significantly more frequent in men than in women in the cohort.
No significant difference was found in the frequency of aortic dissections between men and women.
Spontaneous pneumothorax occurred significantly more frequently in men compared with women.
Overall, 52% of the cohort (74/142) experienced a major vascular, GI, or obstetric event during the study period, most commonly among those with a glycine substitution.

Prior studies cited in the discussion reported celiprolol decreased vascular complications and improved survival in vEDS, but the authors note these studies had design limitations precluding firm conclusions.

Aortic aneurysms/dissections occurred more frequently than middle-sized artery aneurysms/dissections in this cohort, contrary to prior literature identifying MSAs as the main location of vascular complications, likely due to ascertainment bias and incomplete abdominal imaging.
Estimated minimal prevalence of vEDS in the Netherlands was calculated as approximately 1.1 per 100,000, consistent with prior US prevalence estimates.
Early postoperative outcomes including length of hospital stay, discharge disposition, ER visits, and 3-month readmission rates did not significantly differ between EDS and non-EDS THA patients.
Patients with EDS undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty had a significantly higher overall revision rate compared to non-EDS patients (15.0% vs 3.2%).
Revision-free survival after primary THA was significantly lower in EDS patients than non-EDS patients at 9-year follow-up.
Cox proportional hazard regression showed EDS patients had a 7-times higher risk of THA revision compared to non-EDS patients.
Revision due to instability trended higher but was not statistically significant in the EDS cohort compared to non-EDS patients.
During horse-serum-induced myogenic differentiation of C2C12 mouse myoblasts, Zip13 mRNA was upregulated, occurring after the upregulation of the myogenic regulatory factors MyoD and Myogenin.

shRNA-mediated knockdown of Zip13 in C2C12 cells suppressed myotube formation and reduced expression of the myogenic markers MyoD, Myogenin, Myf5, Myh2, and MYH protein compared with scrambled-shRNA control cells.

Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were successfully generated from two EDSSPD3 patients harboring the ZIP13G64D mutation, showing normal morphology, ALP activity, and pluripotency markers (SSEA4, TRA-1-81) equivalent to healthy controls while retaining the original mutation.

During DOX-induced myogenic differentiation, mRNA and protein expression of endogenous MYOD and Myogenin were significantly lower in EDSSPD3-iPSC-derived myocytes compared with healthy control-iPSC-derived myocytes.
Western blot analysis showed lower MYH protein levels in myocytes differentiated from EDSSPD3-P2-iPSCsMYOD compared with control iPSC-derived myocytes.

Baseline (Day 0) expression of the zinc-status marker hMT1H was significantly higher in undifferentiated EDSSPD3 patient iPSCs than in healthy control iPSCs, suggesting disrupted intracellular zinc status due to the ZIP13G64D mutation.
hCK-M and hPAX3 mRNA expression were significantly downregulated in myocytes derived from EDSSPD3-iPSCsMYOD on Day 8 compared with healthy controls.

CRISPR-Cas9/ssODN-mediated homology-directed repair correction of the ZIP13G64D mutation in patient iPSCs (clones RC1-3) restored hMYOGENIN mRNA and protein expression during myogenic differentiation compared with uncorrected EDSSPD3-P1-iPSCsMYOD.

ZIP13 is reported to be involved in BMP/TGF-β-mediated signaling pathways, which is proposed as a mechanism underlying the diverse phenotypes seen in Zip13-KO mice and patients with EDSSPD3 harboring ZIP13G64D.

Zip13-KO mice and EDSSPD3 patients exhibit reduced white fat mass, previously attributed to accelerated adipocyte browning associated with increased C/EBP-β protein levels, and the authors propose C/EBP-β-mediated repression of myogenesis may also be dysregulated by loss of ZIP13.

The ZIP13G64D mutant protein is readily degraded via the valosin-containing protein (VCP)-linked ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, and this loss of functional ZIP13 protein is considered the main molecular mechanism underlying EDSSPD3 pathogenesis.

Patients with EDSSPD3 (spondylodysplastic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type 3, OMIM 612350) present with muscular symptoms including muscular hypotonia, reduced muscular strength, and myopathy, alongside short stature, skeletal dysplasia, spine deformity, fragile skin, and hypodontia.
Dominant and recessive mutations in COL12A1 cause an Ehlers-Danlos syndrome-like disorder characterized by joint hypermobility, contractures, and abnormal skin healing.

The EDS/Ullrich-overlapping disease caused by COL12A1 mutations, termed myopathic-type EDS (mEDS), presents with muscle contractures, motor dysfunction and weakness overlapping Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy features.
The mEDS phenotype has been closely recapitulated in collagen XII-deficient mice.
Tenascin X deficiency causes a spectrum of mEDS-like disorders that mimic the phenotype of collagen VI related myopathies.
Dominant and recessive mutations in type VI collagen cause a range of muscular dystrophies from Bethlem myopathy (mild) to Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy (severe).
Collagen VI deficiency also affects skin and tendon through abnormal interactions between resident cells and collagen I fibrils, resulting in weakened tissue.
A COL6A6 missense mutation has been associated with retinitis pigmentosa.
A missense mutation in COL6A2 has been associated with progressive myoclonus epilepsy syndrome.
A COL6A5 variant has been associated with chronic itch disorder.
Several collagen VI mutations have been associated with isolated recessive dystonia.
Collagen VI polymorphisms have been linked to atopic dermatitis and corneal biomechanical resistance.
Certain collagen VI polymorphisms have been reported to predispose humans to pathological ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament and osteoarthritis.

Collagen XII and collagen VI colocalize in the pericellular zones of osteoblast cultures and in regenerative axons, and their gene expression is co-regulated in human mesenchymal stem cells and zebrafish, suggesting a functional and stoichiometric relationship between the two collagens.
Dysregulated collagen XII and VI expression predicts aberrant migratory behavior of tumor cells and poor prognosis in colorectal cancer.
TGFBIp deficiency results in aberrant bone growth, supporting a role for the collagen VI/XII/TGFBIp complex in maintaining cellular orientation and osteoblast polarity.
In vitro solid-phase binding assays showed that collagen VI failed to interact directly with tenascin X, suggesting only indirect bridging via SLRPs is possible.

Direct physical interaction between collagen VI and collagen XII has not been demonstrated, and no single accessory protein bridging them has yet been identified, despite overlapping human disease phenotypes.
Among 116 women with knee osteoarthritis, 67.24% showed generalized joint hypermobility, and increasing age was significantly associated with the presence of hypermobility.
Passive dorsiflexion of the right fifth MCP joint increased with age across the four age groups.
Passive dorsiflexion of the left fifth MCP joint likewise increased with age across the four age groups.
Right knee hyperextension increased with age, with the highest proportion (82.6%) seen in the 31-40 year age group.
Left knee hyperextension was also significantly associated with age group.
No significant association was found between age group and the ability to place palms flat on the floor with knees extended.
Overall, BMI category was not significantly associated with generalized joint hypermobility.
Higher BMI was significantly associated with right knee hyperextension specifically, though not with hypermobility overall.
Among the OA patients with hypermobility, the knee joint was the most frequently affected joint, followed by the distal interphalangeal joints.
Whole-body vibration produced no positive acute effect on postural stability (overall stability index) in adults with or without generalized joint hypermobility.

At a 15 Hz vibration frequency, a significant Before-to-After time effect was seen on the stable platform with open eyes in the control-without-vibration group, and on the unstable platform with closed eyes in both GJH+WBV and CTRL+WBV groups.
At 15 Hz, no significant interaction was found between time and group factors for postural stability outcomes.
At a 30 Hz vibration frequency, a significant Before-to-After time effect was observed on the stable platform with open eyes.
At 30 Hz, no significant interaction was found between time and group factors for postural stability.
Toddlers with generalized joint hypermobility (GJH) scored lower on the tactile deep pressure subtest of the Test of Sensory Functions in Infants (TSFI) compared to toddlers without GJH.
Toddlers with GJH scored lower on the adaptive motor functions subtest of the TSFI compared to toddlers without GJH.
Toddlers with GJH scored lower on the visual-tactile integration subtest of the TSFI compared to toddlers without GJH.
Toddlers with GJH scored lower on the response to vestibular stimuli subtest of the TSFI compared to toddlers without GJH.
Total TSFI score was lower in toddlers with GJH than in toddlers without GJH, indicating overall poorer sensory processing.
Some studies reported an association between small fiber neuropathy and central sensitisation in fibromyalgia patients.
Patients with both fibromyalgia and small fiber neuropathy show distinct sensory profiles compared to patients with small fiber neuropathy alone.
Pain-driving IgG antibodies targeting satellite glial cells in the dorsal root ganglia have been identified in a subset of fibromyalgia patients with high symptom severity.
An animal model study confirmed that neuroinflammation at the dorsal root ganglia in fibromyalgia is mediated by polymorphonuclear neutrophils.
Growing evidence links COVID-19 infection to the persistence of fibromyalgia symptoms after recovery.
Research has explored circulating microRNA expression as a potential biomarker to aid fibromyalgia diagnosis.
Clinimetric studies have examined whether primary indices of fibromyalgia disease severity can be used interchangeably, particularly in studies with large case numbers.
Non-invasive brain stimulation has emerged as a novel non-pharmacological therapeutic strategy aimed at relieving symptoms and improving functionality in fibromyalgia patients.
Exercise programs have been highlighted as a non-pharmacological intervention aimed at relieving symptoms and improving functionality in fibromyalgia patients.

A 48-year-old woman with fibromyalgia who self-doubled her pregabalin dose to 300 mg/daily developed resting tremor and bradykinesia (parkinsonism) after 5 days, which fully resolved 7 days after pregabalin discontinuation.

The authors note that only 6 prior cases of pregabalin-induced parkinsonism have been reported in the literature, and in all reported cases full recovery occurred after pregabalin withdrawal, with discontinuation being the most common management strategy.
Pretreatment with the BTK inhibitor acalabrutinib inhibited anti-IgE-mediated histamine release from human skin explants, with an optimal inhibitory concentration of 2.5 µg/ml.
Pertussis toxin, which blocks Gi-protein signaling, inhibited anti-IgE-mediated histamine release in the skin explant model.
The MRGPRX2 antagonist QWF (100 µM) inhibited compound 48/80-mediated histamine release in the skin explant model.
In paired testing of the same donors, compound 48/80 (MRGPRX2 agonist) elicited greater histamine release than anti-IgE (FcɛRI agonist) after a 1-hour stimulation period.
Total skin histamine content varied significantly between and within individual donors and correlated strongly with biopsy tissue weight, though variance persisted after weight correction.
Spontaneous histamine release was directly correlated with total skin histamine content, but as a percentage of total content it rarely exceeded 2% in NDRI specimens.

Washing fresh, same-day surgical skin specimens in EDTA followed by graded increases in calcium concentration reduced spontaneous histamine release to 1.03 ± 0.37% while preserving detectable anti-IgE- and compound 48/80-stimulated histamine release.

Fresh surgical skin specimens processed the same day as surgery exhibited markedly elevated spontaneous histamine release, occasionally exceeding 60% within the first hour post-biopsy, which decreased over subsequent time.
Mast cell-derived PGD2 production was detected in skin explants following anti-IgE stimulation, demonstrating that this model captures synthesized lipid mediator release in addition to histamine.
Anti-IgE-induced histamine release detection was inconsistent at very short (5 min) stimulation times but was reliably detected at 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
No significant difference in histamine release was found between anti-IgE concentrations of 1 µg/ml and 3 µg/ml.
Compound 48/80-mediated histamine release kinetics were similar across 30, 60, and 120 minute stimulation periods.

In this explant model, median stimulated histamine release for 1 µg/ml anti-IgE increased markedly between 20 minutes (4.66%) and 60 minutes (15.75%) of stimulation, comparable to skin tissue homogenate literature values obtained at similarly long stimulation periods.
Quercetin reduced TNF-α expression and secretion in PMA/tBHQ-activated HMC-1 mast cells.

Kaempferol suppressed store-operated calcium entry (SOCE)-mediated Ca2+ influx in HMC-1 cells.

Molecular docking showed quercetin binds ORAI with high affinity at the same binding site as the known ORAI inhibitor YM58483.
Molecular docking showed kaempferol binds ORAI with high affinity at the same binding site as the known ORAI inhibitor YM58483.

Oral kaempferol administered daily for 14 days significantly reversed LPS-induced depression-like behaviors in mice.

Quercetin administration reduced hippocampal mast cell activation in LPS-induced depressive mice.
Kaempferol administration reduced hippocampal mast cell activation in LPS-induced depressive mice.
Serum tryptase levels did not significantly differ between PACS patients, asymptomatic COVID-19 convalescents, and controls without prior COVID-19.

Oral administration of Ampelopsis brevipedunculata ethanol extract (ABE) prevented and significantly suppressed OVA-induced hypothermia in the active systemic anaphylaxis (ASA) mouse model.

ABE reduced OVA-induced elevation of serum total IgE in a dose-dependent manner in the ASA model.
ABE reduced OVA-specific IgE levels in serum in a dose-dependent manner in the ASA model.
ABE reduced serum IL-4 levels in a dose-dependent manner in the ASA model.
Oral ABE suppressed Evans blue dye extravasation, a measure of vascular permeability, in the IgE-mediated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis (PCA) mouse model.
ABE suppressed the IgE-mediated increase in ear thickness in the passive cutaneous anaphylaxis (PCA) model.
ABE significantly inhibited IgE/antigen-induced histamine release from three types of mast cells (RBL-2H3, rat peritoneal mast cells, and bone marrow-derived mast cells).
ABE significantly inhibited IgE/antigen-induced β-hexosaminidase release from RBL-2H3, RPMCs, and BMMCs mast cells.

ABE markedly inhibited both gene expression and secretion of IL-4 in IgE-activated mast cells.
ABE suppressed IκBα degradation and nuclear translocation of NF-κB in IgE-activated mast cells, indicating inhibition of NF-κB pathway activation as a mechanism for its anti-inflammatory effect.
ABE showed no cytotoxicity in RBL-2H3 mast cells at concentrations up to 100 µg/mL, supporting the safety of concentrations used in subsequent experiments.
Among ABE's constituent compounds tested (catechin, gallic acid, resveratrol), gallic acid showed the greatest inhibitory effect on mast cell activation markers, per supplementary data.
CD300f-deficient mice showed significantly increased sneezing frequency compared to wild-type mice after nasal ragweed pollen challenge in an allergic rhinitis model.
CD300f deficiency did not significantly alter serum ragweed-specific IgE levels compared with wild-type mice after allergen challenge.
Nasal mast cell numbers were comparable between WT and CD300f-deficient mice regardless of allergen challenge status.
The percentage of degranulated nasal mast cells was higher in CD300f-deficient mice than wild-type mice after allergen challenge, indicating CD300f normally restrains mast cell degranulation.
Mast cell-deficient KitW-sh/W-sh mice showed profoundly reduced sneezing frequency compared with WT mice in the same allergic rhinitis model, confirming mast cell dependency of the sneezing symptom.
CD300f-deficient mice exhibited higher numbers and higher percentages of degranulated eosinophils in nasal tissue than WT mice after allergen challenge.

CD300f was highly expressed on mast cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils in nasal tissue under steady-state conditions, with surface expression slightly increased in mast cells and eosinophils after allergen challenge.

Blocking endogenous ceramide with an anti-ceramide antibody increased sneezing frequency and increased mast cell degranulation but did not affect serum IgE, mast cell numbers, or eosinophil numbers, supporting a CD300f-ceramide inhibitory axis in vivo.

Ceramide antibody treatment increased degranulated mast cell numbers but did not significantly alter mast cell or eosinophil counts or serum RW-specific IgE, indicating a selective effect on degranulation.

Ceramide liposomes inhibited IgE-mediated degranulation of wild-type bone marrow-derived mast cells but had no effect on CD300f-deficient BMMCs, confirming that ceramide liposomes act through CD300f in vitro.
Intravenous ceramide liposome administration reduced the percentage of nasal mast cell degranulation but did not affect serum IgE levels or nasal mast cell/eosinophil numbers.
Intranasal administration of ceramide liposomes reduced sneezing frequency and the numbers of degranulated mast cells and eosinophils in nasal mucosa in the allergic rhinitis model.
Intranasal ceramide liposome treatment did not significantly change serum RW-specific IgE levels or nasal mast cell numbers.

Intranasal corticosteroid (fluticasone propionate) reduced sneezing frequency, degranulated mast cells, and eosinophils in nasal tissue similarly to ceramide liposomes, without affecting serum IgE or mast cell numbers.
Intranasal ceramide liposomes failed to reduce sneezing frequency in CD300f-deficient mice, demonstrating that the therapeutic effect requires CD300f.
Intranasal phosphatidylserine liposomes had no effect on sneezing frequency or on the numbers of degranulated mast cells and eosinophils in nasal tissue, unlike ceramide liposomes.
Intranasal ceramide liposomes reduced sneezing frequency in a dose-dependent manner across 0.2, 0.6, and 2 μg doses.
Intranasal ceramide liposomes reduced the elevated sneezing frequency caused by anti-ceramide antibody treatment, demonstrating a reversal of the antibody-induced exacerbation.
Mast cell-specific (MCPT5-Cre) loss of CD300f enhanced IgE-dependent passive cutaneous anaphylaxis (dye extravasation) responses compared with control CD300fflox/flox mice.

Mast cell-specific loss of CD300f increased sneezing frequency, mast cell degranulation, and eosinophil numbers in nasal tissue in the allergic rhinitis model, while serum IgE and mast cell numbers were unaffected, indicating nasal mast cell-expressed CD300f is critical for suppressing AR development.
Untargeted plasma metabolomics revealed clear overall differences in metabolite profiles between patients with chronic urticaria and healthy controls.

A four-metabolite panel (N6-acetyl-L-lysine, L-aspartate, maleic acid, and pyruvic acid) used in random forest classifiers distinguished CU patients from healthy controls with AUC values greater than 0.85, suggesting diagnostic biomarker potential.

Low plasma pyruvic acid was significantly associated with higher chronic urticaria disease activity, poorer response to second-generation H1 antihistamines, and shorter relapse-free time, with the association validated in an independent cohort.

Low plasma maleic acid was significantly associated with higher chronic urticaria disease activity, poorer response to second-generation H1 antihistamines, and shorter relapse-free time, with the association validated in an independent cohort.
Low plasma pyruvic acid levels were significantly associated with shorter relapse-free time in patients with chronic urticaria, indicating prognostic value.
Low plasma maleic acid levels were significantly associated with shorter relapse-free time in patients with chronic urticaria, mirroring the pyruvic acid finding.
Supplementation with pyruvate significantly attenuated IgE-mediated mast cell activation in bone marrow-derived mast cells in vitro.
Supplementation with maleate significantly attenuated IgE-mediated mast cell activation in bone marrow-derived mast cells in vitro.
In a mouse model of IgE-induced passive cutaneous anaphylaxis, pyruvate or maleate supplementation significantly attenuated the anaphylactic response in vivo.
The diagnostic and prognostic metabolite associations identified in the discovery cohort were confirmed in an independent validation cohort of 144 chronic urticaria patients.
A positive mast cell activation status was significantly more common in perioperative anaphylaxis cases with an identifiable suspected causal agent compared with those without.
An elevated median serum acute tryptase level did not predict identification of the suspected causal agent in perioperative anaphylaxis.
Positive urinary mast cell mediator metabolites were not associated with identification of the suspected causal agent during perioperative anaphylaxis.
Patients with positive urinary mast cell mediator metabolites had significantly higher median serum acute tryptase levels than those with negative urinary metabolites.
Patients with positive urinary mast cell mediator metabolites had significantly higher rates of positive mast cell activation status than those with negative urinary metabolites.
Patients with perioperative anaphylaxis showed an elevated acute-to-baseline urinary 11β-prostaglandin-F2α ratio above 1.6.
Patients with perioperative anaphylaxis showed an elevated acute-to-baseline urinary N-methylhistamine ratio above 1.7.
Patients with perioperative anaphylaxis showed an elevated acute-to-baseline urinary leukotriene E4 ratio above 1.8.
Peripheral neuropathy (large and/or small fiber) was diagnosed in 60% of alcohol-dependent inpatients based on neurophysiological testing and clinical signs/symptoms.
Among the 54 subjects with neuropathy, pure large fiber neuropathy (LFN) was identified in 18 subjects.
Pure small fiber neuropathy (SFN) was identified in 12 of the 54 subjects with neuropathy.
Combined large and small fiber neuropathy was diagnosed in 24 of the 54 subjects with neuropathy, indicating a symmetrical, length-dependent pattern of nerve involvement.
Higher NSS and NIS clinical scores correlated with lower sural sensory nerve action potential amplitudes and lower sympathetic skin response amplitudes on linear regression.
Subjects with neuropathy had a significantly longer duration of alcohol abuse than those without, per Student's t-test.
An NIS cut-off score of ≥4 predicted large fiber neuropathy with high sensitivity (95.23%) and specificity (93.75%) on ROC analysis.
An NIS cut-off score of ≥4 predicted large fiber neuropathy with 95.23% sensitivity and 93.75% specificity on ROC analysis.
Peripheral neuropathy in AUD patients typically presented with a symmetrical, length-dependent pattern involving both large and small nerve fibers.
The authors suggest that NSS and NIS clinical scales could substitute for neurophysiological testing in assessing neuropathy when such testing is unavailable.
In 37% of patients, the SFN diagnosis was confirmed by both an abnormal intra-epidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) and abnormal quantitative sensory testing (QST).
Patients with SFN had a significantly higher one-way travel distance to the diagnostic center than patients without SFN.
The median HADS anxiety score in the SFN population was 7.0, differing significantly between patient groups.
General health status was rated as bad or moderate in 72% of patients with SFN.
Almost 70% of all patients were not or only a little satisfied with the waiting time until neurological analysis, which averaged 10.5 months.
Overall patient satisfaction with the diagnostic SFN service was high, with a mean satisfaction score of 8.7 (IQR 8–10) on a 0–10 scale.
Multivariate regression found no statistically significant associations between age, sex, education level, anxiety, or depression scores and overall patient satisfaction.
General health status was significantly associated with overall patient satisfaction with the diagnostic SFN service.
Patients without SFN were significantly less satisfied with accessibility to the NDCU/OC, the attending staff member, and the expertise of the doctor performing NCS/QST compared to patients with SFN.
Patients with SFN were significantly less satisfied about the 7–8 week waiting period for receiving their results compared to patients without SFN.
Nearly 45% of all patients were not or only a little satisfied with the 7–8 week waiting period for receiving their neurological analysis results.
Nearly 25% of patients were not or only a little satisfied with the discussion of both medicines and other treatments during their consultation.
The SFN-PSQ demonstrated high feasibility, with 95% (98/103) of approached patients completing the questionnaire in an average of 14 minutes.
Almost 87% of patients with SFN were evaluated during the one-day stay at the neurological day care unit (NDCU) rather than the outpatient clinic, a significant difference in care pathway.

Electroacupuncture reduced the number of mast cells in colon tissue of IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats.
Electroacupuncture lowered Tryptase expression in IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats.
Electroacupuncture lowered PAR-2 (protease-activated receptor-2) expression in IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats.
Electroacupuncture lowered myosin light chain kinase (MLCK) expression in IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats.
Electroacupuncture increased zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) expression in IBS-D rats, indicating restored tight junction protein levels.
Electroacupuncture increased Occludin expression in IBS-D rats, indicating restored tight junction protein levels.
Electroacupuncture reduced the loose stool rate in IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats after 7 days of intervention.
Electroacupuncture improved the minimum volume threshold of abdominal withdrawal reflex (AWR), indicating reduced visceral hypersensitivity, compared to untreated IBS-D rats.

Colon tissue inflammation, assessed by histological examination, was decreased in EA-treated IBS-D rats compared to untreated IBS-D rats.

Keratinocytes in vitally (antemortem) injured skin showed positive TGF-β1 immunohistochemical staining (score 2-3), whereas postmortal and non-injured control samples showed negative or weak staining (score 0-1), a statistically significant difference.
Some vitally injured skin samples additionally showed dermal (not just keratinocyte) TGF-β1 expression.
Dermal mast cell density, assessed via tryptase immunohistochemistry, showed no significant difference between vital injury, postmortal injury, and control non-injured groups.
Patients with a cyclic pattern of gastroparesis symptoms had significantly higher rates of diabetes mellitus compared to those with a non-cyclic pattern.
A cyclic symptom pattern was associated with lower odds of achieving at least a 1-point improvement in vomiting after temporary mucosal gastric stimulation, in univariable analysis.
After adjusting for sex and age-squared, a cyclic symptom pattern remained significantly associated with lower odds of vomiting improvement following temporary gastric stimulation.
Patients who improved with gastric stimulation had a higher mucosal electrogastrogram frequency-to-amplitude ratio (FAR) than those who did not improve.
Cyclic and non-cyclic gastroparesis symptom groups did not differ significantly in personal or familial history of dysautonomia patterns.
Overall, roughly half of gastroparesis patients showed at least a 1-point symptom improvement after temporary mucosal gastric stimulation, while the other half did not.
CCN2 protein expression score in megakaryocytes of the whole MPN group was not significantly different from normal control bone marrow.
No correlation was found between CCN2 protein expression score and the degree of bone marrow fibrosis in MPN patients.
A subgroup of 7 of 55 MPN cases (13%) showed marked megakaryocytic CCN2 overexpression compared to the rest of the cohort.
JAK2 V617F variant allele frequency did not significantly correlate with CCN2 expression score in the MPN cases with CCN2 overexpression.
CCN2 expression score did not significantly differ among MPN disease subgroups (ET, PV, PMF, post-ET MF, post-PV MF, pre-PMF).

The authors propose that noncanonical, JNK-dependent (rather than canonical SMAD2/3-mediated) TGF-beta signaling in mesenchymal stromal cells, independent of CCN2, likely drives bone marrow fibrosis in MPN.
Subcutaneous (peripheral) administration of histamine did not alter LPS-induced colonic hyperpermeability in rats.
Intracisternal (central) administration of histamine improved LPS-induced colonic hyperpermeability in rats.
Elevating endogenous brain histamine with the histamine N-methyltransferase inhibitor SKF91488 improved colonic hyperpermeability.
Intracisternal chlorpheniramine, an H1 receptor antagonist, abolished the SKF91488-induced improvement in colonic hyperpermeability, implicating histamine H1 receptor signaling.
Intracisternal ranitidine, an H2 receptor antagonist, did not block the SKF91488-induced improvement in colonic hyperpermeability, indicating H2 receptor is not involved.
Vagotomy blocked the SKF91488-induced improvement in colonic hyperpermeability, implicating the vagus nerve in this brain-to-gut pathway.

Blocking adenosine A2B receptors with intracisternal alloxazine abolished the SKF91488-induced improvement in colonic hyperpermeability, indicating that A2B receptor signaling downstream of basal forebrain cholinergic neuron activity is required for the brain histamine-mediated barrier effect.

Intracisternal chlorpheniramine (an H1 receptor antagonist) eliminated the butyrate-induced improvement in colonic hyperpermeability, linking brain histamine H1 receptor signaling to the previously identified butyrate-BFCN gut barrier pathway.
A high combined weighted gastrointestinal symptom score (CWSS) was associated with higher odds of diabetic autonomic neuropathy as measured by COMPASS-31.
In type 1 diabetes, participants with high gastrointestinal symptom burden had higher odds of cardiac autonomic neuropathy assessed by cardiac autonomic reflex tests (CARTs).

In type 1 diabetes, high gastrointestinal symptom burden was associated with higher odds of distal symmetrical polyneuropathy (DSPN) as detected by vibration perception threshold (VPT) and the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI).

In type 2 diabetes, high gastrointestinal symptom burden was associated with higher odds of distal symmetrical polyneuropathy as detected by electrochemical skin conductance (ESC), vibration perception threshold, and pain sensation testing.
A high gastrointestinal combined weighted symptom score was present in 25% of participants with type 1 diabetes and 38% of participants with type 2 diabetes.
Gastrointestinal symptom burden showed inconsistent associations with different neuropathy tests when comparing type 1 and type 2 diabetes cohorts.
Knockout of the Trpv1 gene in mice significantly reduced their ability to sense and respond to colorectal distension.
A TRPV1 antagonist blunted visceromotor responses to colorectal distension in rat models of colonic hypersensitivity.
The number of TRPV1-positive nerve fibers is elevated in colonic biopsies of patients with IBS compared with healthy controls.
TRPV1 transcription levels and protein immunoreactivity correlate positively with abdominal pain scores in patients with IBS.
TRPV1-positive neuronal fibers were 5-fold higher in colorectal biopsies from quiescent IBD patients with ongoing abdominal pain compared with those without pain.
In multivariate analysis, TRPV1 positivity was the only covariate significantly associated with abdominal pain score in these patients.

Germ-free rats inoculated with fecal microbiota from IBS-C patients with visceral hypersensitivity showed increased abdominal contractions on colorectal distension compared with rats given healthy-donor microbiota.
Guinea pig submucosal neurons exposed to colon supernatants from IBS-C patients showed increased neuronal activation measured by spike discharge.
Enteric and DRG neuronal responses to colon supernatants were more pronounced when derived from IBS patients with visceral hypersensitivity than from those with normosensitivity.
The number of activated mast cells and their proximity to colonic neurons was significantly increased in the colonic mucosa of IBS patients compared with healthy controls.
The number of mast cells proximal to colonic nerves positively correlates with the severity of abdominal pain or discomfort in IBS.

Pro-nociceptive mast cell mediators (histamine, tryptase, prostaglandin E2, prostaglandin D2), each of which sensitizes TRPV1, are elevated in the colonic mucosa of IBS patients compared with healthy controls.
Serum and plasma IL-6 levels are significantly elevated in patients with IBS relative to healthy controls.
Blockade of IL-6 signaling decreased visceral hypersensitivity in a rat model of IBS, shown by an increased pain threshold for colorectal distension.

IBS patients with increased intestinal permeability (lactulose-to-mannitol ratio ≥0.07) had significantly higher visceral pain scores on colorectal distension than IBS patients with normal permeability (<0.07).

Colonic biopsy supernatants from IBS patients increase paracellular permeability of cultured colonic epithelial cells, and the degree of induced permeability correlates with severity of patient-reported abdominal pain.

In rats, tenapanor produced dose-dependent increases in stool sodium content and luminal fluid retention, with sustained increases over 4 days of repeated dosing that returned to baseline upon discontinuation.
In healthy volunteers, tenapanor 15-60 mg BID increased stool sodium retention by 20-50 mmol/day and increased stool frequency and weight relative to placebo, without affecting serum/plasma sodium.
Tenapanor's sodium-retention effects are limited to the gut lumen with no impact on serum/plasma sodium levels.
Oral tenapanor 0.5 mg/kg BID significantly reduced visceromotor responses to colorectal distension in acetic acid-sensitized rats, comparable to naive (non-sensitized) rats.

In single-cell patch-clamp experiments in colon-specific DRG from acetic acid-sensitized rats, tenapanor reversed DRG hyperexcitability following capsaicin (TRPV1 agonist) exposure, suggesting normalization of TRPV1-mediated nociceptive signaling.
In studies with human colonic epithelial monolayers, tenapanor reduced intestinal cell permeability to macromolecules.
In the T3MPO-1 phase 3 trial, significantly more patients on tenapanor 50 mg BID met the combined abdominal pain/CSBM primary endpoint than those on placebo (27.0% vs 18.7%).
In the T3MPO-2 phase 3 trial (26 weeks), significantly more patients on tenapanor 50 mg BID met the primary endpoint than those on placebo (36.5% vs 23.7%).

Significantly more tenapanor-treated patients than placebo-treated patients experienced durable improvement in abdominal pain across the first 12 weeks (both trials) and this was sustained further in secondary analyses at 6/12, 9/12, and 13/26 week thresholds.

Among 186 T3MPO-2 patients on tenapanor for the full 26-week treatment period, the proportion reporting moderate-to-severe abdominal pain fell from 100% at baseline to 38% at week 26, with 31% reporting no pain.

Diarrhea was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event with tenapanor across the phase 3 trials (14.6% in T3MPO-1, 16.0% in T3MPO-2, 11.1% in T3MPO-3), was usually transient (resolving within a week), mild-to-moderate, and associated with a low (<10%) discontinuation rate.
Tenapanor inhibits the NHE3 sodium/hydrogen exchanger, reducing intestinal sodium absorption and increasing luminal water retention, which accelerates transit and softens stool.

In rats, single oral doses of tenapanor produced dose-dependent increases in stool sodium and luminal fluid retention, with repeated dosing sustaining the effect until it returned to baseline upon discontinuation.
In healthy volunteers, twice-daily tenapanor 15-60 mg increased stool sodium retention by 20-50 mmol/day, equivalent to 2.8 g of table salt.
Tenapanor administration in healthy volunteers increased stool frequency and stool weight relative to placebo.
Tenapanor's sodium retention effects are limited to the gut and do not affect serum or plasma sodium levels.

In a rat model of acetic acid-induced colonic hypersensitivity, oral tenapanor significantly reduced visceromotor responses to colorectal distension compared with vehicle, to levels comparable with naive rats.
Tenapanor reversed capsaicin-induced dorsal root ganglion hyperexcitability in colon-specific DRG from acetic acid-sensitized rats, suggesting normalization of TRPV1-mediated nociceptive signaling.
In human colonic epithelial monolayers, tenapanor reduced intestinal cell permeability to macromolecules.

In the T3MPO-1 phase 3 trial, significantly more IBS-C patients on tenapanor 50 mg BID met the primary composite endpoint of abdominal pain response plus increased bowel movements than those on placebo.
In the T3MPO-2 phase 3 trial, significantly more IBS-C patients on tenapanor 50 mg BID met the primary composite endpoint than those on placebo.
Proportionally more tenapanor-treated patients than placebo had a clinically meaningful abdominal pain response for ≥6 of the first 12 weeks in both T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2.
Significantly more tenapanor-treated patients than placebo had abdominal pain response for ≥9 of the first 12 weeks of treatment in both T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2.
In T3MPO-2, significantly more tenapanor-treated patients than placebo had an abdominal pain response for ≥13 of 26 weeks of treatment.

Significantly more tenapanor-treated patients experienced durable improvements in abdominal pain (≥30% reduction for ≥9 of first 12 weeks including ≥3 weeks during weeks 8-12) than placebo in both trials.
At each week of the 12-week T3MPO-1 and 26-week T3MPO-2 trials, tenapanor 50 mg BID produced statistically significant reductions in mean abdominal pain score compared with placebo.
Among 186 T3MPO-2 patients treated with tenapanor for 26 weeks, the proportion reporting moderate-to-severe abdominal pain fell from 100% at baseline to 38% at week 26, with 31% reporting no pain.
Tenapanor also alleviated other IBS-C abdominal symptoms including bloating, discomfort, cramping, and fullness.
Diarrhea was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event in tenapanor-treated patients across the T3MPO trials.
Most diarrhea episodes associated with tenapanor were transient, resolving within 1 week, and of mild or moderate severity, with a low (<10%) rate of treatment discontinuation.
Based on T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2 efficacy and safety data, tenapanor was approved by the US FDA in 2019 for treatment of adults with IBS-C.
In 2022, the American Gastroenterological Association endorsed tenapanor for treatment of IBS-C in its clinical practice guideline, based on the certainty of scientific evidence.
Of 200 presumptive ME/CFS cases identified by ICD diagnosis codes, only 3% were confirmed and 12% probable ME/CFS on chart review, while 19% were possible and 60% did not meet ME/CFS criteria.
Confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases were predominantly female (76.6%) and White (96.6%).

The overall crude annual rate of first ME/CFS diagnosis code entry among 9- to 39-year-olds in the Kaiser Permanente Northwest population from 2006-2017 was 21.5 per 100,000 person-years (455 index cases).
ME/CFS diagnosis coding rates increased with age, from 5.2 per 100,000 person-years among 9-19 year olds to 37.0 per 100,000 among 30-39 year olds.
Females had substantially higher ME/CFS diagnosis coding rates than males across all age groups (32 vs 9.7 per 100,000 person-years overall).
ME/CFS diagnosis coding rates rose substantially between 2006 and 2017 in all age groups, most sharply among 30-39 year old females (29.1 to 93.3 per 100,000 person-years).
Chronic pain, major depression, and anxiety disorders were the most common comorbid conditions among confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases.
Among confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases with chronic pain, fibromyalgia was the sole cause in 7%, another cause alone in 30%, and both fibromyalgia and another cause in 43%.
Most confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases (90%) received prescriptions for medications that can contribute to fatigue, including opioids (73%) and other sedating drug classes (66%).
Common fatigue-targeting medications prescribed to confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases included stimulants (30%), bupropion (20%), and modafinil/armodafinil (17%).

Confirmed/probable ME/CFS cases commonly underwent broad laboratory workup, most frequently complete blood count (100%), thyroid function (98%), and vitamin B12 (96%), often repeated multiple times over years.

Key ME/CFS-relevant diagnostic tests for sleep and orthostatic intolerance were underused: only 43% of confirmed/probable cases had polysomnography or a home sleep test, and only 10% underwent tilt table testing.
Naturopath referral was more common among possible/not-ME/CFS cases (29%) than confirmed/probable cases (17%), but this difference was not statistically significant.
Diagnosis of ME/CFS via ICD code entry was delayed substantially after symptom onset, with a median delay of 5 years and mean of 7.3 years.
Repeated ME/CFS code entries over longer time periods improved diagnostic accuracy; six code entries over 5 years yielded 84% specificity and 70% sensitivity for chart-confirmed/probable ME/CFS.
Family history of ME/CFS or fibromyalgia was rarely documented in the EHR, but among those queried, some reported affected family members.
NK cells from ME/CFS patients show decreased TRPM3-mediated calcium influx, indicating a loss-of-function channelopathy.
TRPM3 channel dysfunction (reduced calcium influx in NK cells) has also been observed in Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) patients.
Low-dose naltrexone has been shown to improve TRPM3 channel function (increase calcium influx) in NK cells both in vitro and in vivo.
Naltrexone, as a µ-opioid receptor antagonist, is proposed to counteract inhibitory effects of the µ-opioid receptor on TRPM3, restoring channel activity.
TRPM3 currents in NK cells from ME/CFS patients were resistant to the antagonist ononetin in the presence of the agonists pregnenolone and nifedipine, indicating channel dysfunction.

Two disease-associated TRPM3 variants cause a gain-of-function with increased basal channel activity, leading to cellular calcium overload and neurodevelopmental symptoms including intellectual disability, epilepsy, musculoskeletal anomalies and altered pain perception.
Clinical studies indicate impaired TRPM3 channel activity in patients with post-COVID-19 conditions, suggesting this dysfunction contributes to chronic post-infection symptoms similar to ME/CFS.
Off-label low-dose naltrexone use in clinical studies has shown alleviation of COVID-19-related symptoms including fibromyalgia, fatigue, and pain.
Small nerve fiber degeneration has been consistently observed in some patients with ME/CFS and Post-COVID Syndrome.

A recent study reported higher latency for warmth perception in ME/CFS and PCS patients, indicating disturbed warm sensation but normal cold perception, suggesting functional TRPM3 impairment rather than nerve fiber degeneration.

A magnetic resonance spectroscopy study found significantly elevated levels of glutamate and N-acetyl-aspartate in Long-COVID and ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls, supporting excitatory-inhibitory imbalance possibly related to TRPM3/GABA dysfunction.
Post-exertional malaise, the hallmark ME/CFS symptom, was reported by 100% of both ME/CFS and PCC participants with valid symptom data, with comparable severity and near-comparable frequency.
People with ME/CFS reported a significantly greater total number of symptoms than people with PCC.
Unrefreshed sleep occurring 'all the time' was significantly more common among ME/CFS patients than PCC patients.
Short-term memory loss, muscle weakness, lymphadenopathy and nausea were significantly more prevalent among people with ME/CFS than people with PCC.
Among those experiencing light-headedness or dizziness, people with PCC were more likely to be only mildly affected than people with ME/CFS.
PCC participants were more likely than ME/CFS participants to experience heart palpitations 'most of the time'.

The patient had a low-titer positive ANA that was considered insignificant given the absence of underlying autoimmune processes.

Mast cell mediators including tryptase and histamine are postulated to disrupt connective tissue integrity and promote fibroblast proliferation and collagen production, linking mast cell activation to hEDS.
Population studies in school-age children estimate joint hypermobility prevalence of 30-50%, rising to 64.6% in those up to age 15 and declining to about 20% in adults.

Individuals with Joint Hypermobility Syndrome commonly present with a wide spectrum of additional manifestations including joint instability, chronic pain, fatigue, dysautonomia (hypotension and postural dizziness), anxiety/depression, and gastrointestinal/genitourinary symptoms.
The Five-Part Questionnaire and Beighton Score show sensitivity of 71-84% and specificity of 77-89% for identifying generalized joint hypermobility.
A systematic literature review found the Beighton Score to be a highly reliable tool with substantial to excellent inter-rater and intra-rater consistency across assessors of varying experience.
hEDS patients undergo a prolonged 'diagnostic odyssey' with an average of about 10 misdiagnoses and take an average of 5 years to reach a correct diagnosis.
hEDS patients are frequently misdiagnosed with fibromyalgia due to overlapping musculoskeletal pain and dysautonomic symptoms.
A study of 379 individuals with hEDS found a higher prevalence of concomitant inflammatory rheumatologic conditions compared to the general population.
A retrospective study of 79 volunteers with hEDS/HSD (71% hEDS) found small fiber dysfunction in 70% and reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density in 78% of cases.
Historical thermographic studies found that affected joints in rheumatoid arthritis patients showed a higher Thermographic Index, averaging 3.96, compared to unaffected joints.

In a 12-month follow-up of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis patients, the Heat Distribution Index showed a high correlation with the Ritchie Articular Index, Mallya Score, grip strength, morning stiffness, ESR, CRP, and pain (VAS).

In participant (a) with joint hypermobility reporting bilateral knee pain, infrared thermography revealed statistically significant thermal asymmetry between knees, with more extreme temperatures and greater standard deviation on the left knee despite mean temperatures appearing normal.
In participant (b) with right knee pain, both knees showed loss of the normal thermal gradient but no statistically significant difference in thermal distribution between knees.
In participant (c) with left knee pain, thermal distribution analysis showed a statistically significant increase in thermal variability on the left side compared to the right.

The asymptomatic 16-year-old control without joint hypermobility also showed a statistically significant thermal asymmetry between knees, higher on the right, suggesting thermal asymmetry alone is not specific to hypermobility-related joint pain.
A large reference study (566 thermal images) reported the average temperature of the normal, asymptomatic anterior knee as 29.5 ± 1.6°C.

A patient with joint hypermobility and chronic pain also reported episodic sensations of sudden blood pressure drops with palpitations, malaise, weakness, transient sweating, paresthesias, and chronically cold hands/feet, consistent with dysautonomic features.

A patient with joint hypermobility and chronic pelvic/musculoskeletal pain was also diagnosed with endometriosis, uterine myomatosis, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis-related hypothyroidism as comorbidities.
Joint inflammatory responses are typically attributed to elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha and IL-6.
Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic COL3A1 deletion variant confirming vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in a patient with severe aortic disease.
Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic SMAD3 splice-region variant confirming Loeys-Dietz syndrome in the same patient, involving TGF-β signaling.

The patient's aortic arch aneurysm rapidly degenerated from 3.9 cm to 7.0 cm over four years, alongside a new 4-cm infrarenal aneurysm and 2.7-cm left common iliac aneurysm, reflecting aggressive vascular disease progression in combined LDS/vEDS.

A staged hybrid aortic repair (carotid-subclavian transposition, zone 2 arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk, TEVAR extension, and open thoracoabdominal aneurysm repair) was successfully completed in a patient with combined LDS/vEDS, avoiding the higher morbidity of a single complete repair.

TEVAR extension using tapered Terumo Relay endografts landed within the surgical graft (avoiding oversizing of native dissected aorta) produced excellent aortic remodeling at 6 months, but new degeneration of the distal thoracic aorta developed by 12 months.

Open completion thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair using a bottom-up approach with venous-arterial ECMO for distal/visceral perfusion and felt-reinforced anastomoses was completed successfully with an uncomplicated postoperative course.

Family history was notable for an aortic aneurysm in the patient's grandmother and a son with bilateral clubfoot and bicuspid aortic valve, consistent with heritable aortopathy phenotypes co-occurring across generations.

Induced pluripotent stem cell lines were generated from two vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome patients carrying a missense mutation in COL3A1 (c.226A>G, p.Asn76Asp) that encodes type III collagen, a key component of blood vessels.
The generated vEDS patient-derived iPSC lines exhibited typical iPSC morphology, expressed pluripotency markers, and differentiated into all three germ layers.
Parents of children with EDS described diagnostic delay as a central challenge, reflecting the difficulty of recognizing a rare connective tissue disorder.

Interviews with parents identified three superordinate themes, with interactions with healthcare and education professionals emerging as a central and often difficult aspect of parenting a child with EDS.
The study concludes that raising awareness among health and education professionals and promoting effective parental advocacy skills are needed to better support families of children with EDS.
Patients who had EDS undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of all-cause revision surgery within 10 years compared to matched non-EDS patients.
EDS patients undergoing TKA had a 2.49-fold higher risk of revision due to instability compared to matched non-EDS patients.
EDS patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) had a 2.32-fold higher risk of all-cause revision within 10 years compared to matched non-EDS patients.
EDS patients undergoing THA had a 4.26-fold higher risk of revision due to instability compared to matched non-EDS patients.
EDS patients undergoing THA had a 3.63-fold higher risk of revision due to mechanical loosening compared to matched non-EDS patients.

The authors recommend that surgical technique and implant selection for EDS patients consider increased constraint in TKA and larger femoral heads or dual mobility articulations in THA to mitigate instability risk.
Adolescents with hypermobility had more than twice the odds of having any spinal deformity compared to those without hypermobility.
Hypermobility was associated with a modestly increased odds of mild spinal deformity.
Hypermobility was strongly associated with increased odds of moderate spinal deformity, the strongest association among severity groups.
Hypermobility was associated with markedly increased odds of severe spinal deformity, though slightly lower than for moderate deformity.
In this large cohort, the prevalence of hypermobility (Beighton score ≥5/9) was very low at 0.01% of adolescents.
Spinal deformity was common in the cohort, affecting 10.5% of adolescents, predominantly of mild severity.
Heterozygous Fbn1 C1041G Marfan syndrome model mice showed significantly reduced aortic rupture force compared with wild-type mice across all three thoracic aortic segments.
Aortic stretch (a proxy for aortic diameter) at 5 mN and maximum force did not differ significantly between Fbn1+/C1041G and wild-type mice in any of the three segments at 10 weeks of age.

Both untreated and losartan-treated Fbn1mgR/mgR mice showed significantly decreased aortic rupture force in all three segments compared with untreated wild-type mice, indicating losartan did not strengthen the weakened aortic wall.
Four weeks of losartan treatment did not significantly alter aortic rupture force (S1-S3) in Fbn1mgR/mgR mice, despite being a well-known AGTR1 inhibitor used clinically in Marfan syndrome.

Losartan treatment reduced ascending aortic (S1) stretch at both 5 mN and maximum force in Fbn1mgR/mgR mice regardless of sex, indicating a beneficial effect on aortic diameter/elastic properties even though rupture force was unchanged.
The mortality rate of losartan-treated Fbn1mgR/mgR mice (8.3%) was not significantly lower than that of untreated Fbn1mgR/mgR mice (11.8%) during the 4-week treatment period.

Untreated Fbn1mgR/mgR mice showed significantly increased S1 (ascending aortic) stretch at both 5 mN and maximum force compared with wild-type mice, an effect more pronounced in males, consistent with known sex differences in Marfan syndrome outcomes.

Smooth-muscle-specific Efemp2 (fibulin-4) knockout mice, modeling cutis laxa type 1B, showed significantly reduced aortic rupture force in the ascending aorta (S1) but no difference in the descending aorta (S2, S3) compared with wild-type mice.
SMKO mice showed increased stretch of the ascending aorta (S1) at both 5 mN and maximum force but decreased stretch of the descending aorta (S3) at maximum force compared with wild-type mice.
Increased ascending aortic (S1) stretch at 5 mN was associated with lower aortic rupture force in SMKO mice, linking aortic dilation to reduced biomechanical strength.

A CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in mouse model carrying the human-equivalent LTBP1 variant showed no significant difference in aortic rupture force across all three segments in hetero-, homo-, or wild-type mice at 1 year of age, and no mice died of aortic rupture.

A CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in mouse model carrying the human-equivalent MFAP4 variant showed no significant difference in aortic rupture force across all three segments in hetero-, homo-, or wild-type mice at 1 year of age, and no mice died of aortic rupture.

A CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in mouse model carrying the human-equivalent TIMP1 variant showed no significant difference in aortic rupture force across all three segments in hetero-, homo-, hemizygous, or wild-type mice at 1 year of age, and no mice died of aortic rupture.

Compared with the previously reported Col3a1 m1Lsmi vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (vEDS) mouse model, both Fbn1 C1041G and Fbn1 mgR Marfan syndrome models had significantly higher (less impaired) aortic rupture force in all three segments, consistent with the higher mortality rate of the vEDS model.

SMKO (cutis laxa type 1B) mice had ascending aortic (S1) rupture force values comparable to or lower than the vEDS (Col3a1 m1Lsmi) model, while descending aortic (S2, S3) rupture force was comparable to the Marfan syndrome (Fbn1) models.
Orofacial pain was reported far more frequently by JFS patients than by healthy controls.
Pain elicited on palpation of the temporomandibular joint was significantly more common in JFS patients than controls.

Pain intensity measured by the Numerical Rating Scale significantly decreased after six sessions of transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion blockade compared with pretreatment levels.

Fibromyalgia prevalence estimates in the literature range from 0.4% to 8% of the population.
Comorbid depression and/or anxiety is reported in 60-80% of people with fibromyalgia.
Fibromyalgia populations show markedly high rates of lifetime and particularly childhood trauma.
Women are significantly more likely than men to be affected by fibromyalgia.
Fibromyalgia is associated with a hyperexcitable central nervous system reflected by high levels of glutamate.
Serotonin neurotransmitter expression is dysregulated in fibromyalgia.
Dopamine neurotransmitter expression is dysregulated in fibromyalgia.

First-line pharmacological (antidepressants, anticonvulsants, opioids) and non-pharmacological (physiotherapy, pain management, CBT) treatments for fibromyalgia show at best moderate efficacy, and often fail to adequately address comorbid mental health symptoms.

Classic psychedelics act primarily as 5-HT2A receptor agonists (with additional 5-HT1A/1C/2C and indirect dopaminergic action), which dysregulates population-level neural oscillations and is linked to markers of anatomical neuroplasticity.
The study's primary EEG hypothesis (H1) is that Lempel-Ziv complexity of resting-state EEG signal will increase at peak psilocybin drug effect in fibromyalgia patients.
The study's primary fMRI hypothesis (H2) is that brain network modularity will decrease after psychedelic-assisted therapy in fibromyalgia patients.

Serum TREM-1 levels were significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls.

No significant between-group differences were found for secondary outcomes including quality of life, fibromyalgia impact, physical function, fatigue, pain catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, and positive-negative affect.
During standing, fibromyalgia patients showed higher total peripheral resistance than healthy women.
During standing, fibromyalgia patients showed lower stroke volume than healthy women.
During standing, fibromyalgia patients showed lower cardiac output than healthy women.
During standing, fibromyalgia patients showed lower baroreflex sensitivity than healthy women.

The patient's longstanding history of Sjogren's syndrome, fibromyalgia, and dystonia may have contributed to the development of idiopathic avascular necrosis (Preiser's disease) of the scaphoid.

Non-surgical treatments for Preiser's disease (NSAIDs, corticosteroid or hyaluronic acid injections, immobilization) have not shown efficacy in preventing osseous deterioration or improving range of motion, grip strength, wrist pain, or radiographic progression.
Corticosteroid injections may further disrupt blood supply to the scaphoid and are relatively contraindicated in suspected Preiser's disease.

A meta-analysis of 138 Preiser's disease cases found that stage II disease is best managed with vascularized bone grafting and closing radial wedge osteotomy in the absence of radiocarpal osteoarthritis, while surgical management evidence for stage I is inconclusive.

Proximal row carpectomy performed for this patient's stage III/IV Preiser's disease resulted in postoperative pain relief and improved wrist function, with limited but improved (to baseline) range of motion.
Presence of autosomal mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), especially two or more, was associated with increased risk of incident cirrhosis.
Individuals carrying copy-number-neutral mCAs (CN-LOH) had a significantly higher risk of developing cirrhosis compared to non-carriers.
CN-LOH was significantly associated with an increased risk of compensated cirrhosis, while its effect on decompensated cirrhosis was only marginally significant.
Expanded mCAs (cell fraction ≥10%) showed a much stronger association with cirrhosis risk than non-expanded mCAs.
Expanded CN-LOH mCAs showed a much stronger association with decompensated cirrhosis risk than non-expanded CN-LOH mCAs.
A 12-SNP cirrhosis polygenic risk score showed a graded, dose-response association with incident cirrhosis risk, with higher genetic risk conferring greater risk.
Individuals carrying mCAs combined with high genetic risk had the highest risk of developing cirrhosis, indicating a synergistic joint effect of mCAs and PRS.
Individuals with expanded CN-LOH and high genetic risk showed the highest cirrhosis risk among all mCA-PRS combinations examined.
Among individuals with expanded mCAs and high genetic risk, the incidence rate of cirrhosis was over four times that of individuals without mCAs and low genetic risk.
For expanded gain abnormalities with intermediate genetic risk, an additive interaction between mCA and PRS accounted for the vast majority of cirrhosis risk in that group.
No significant interaction effect was found between PRS and autosomal mCAs on the risk of compensated cirrhosis.
Prevalence of autosomal mCAs increased notably with advancing age, being higher in participants aged 65 years or older compared to younger participants.
The review states that mast cell activation syndrome involves an increased number of mast cells due to decreased cell death, leading to multi-system clinical symptoms.
The review reports the main common symptoms of mast cell activation syndrome as flushing, hypotension, urticaria, angioedema, headache, vomiting, and diarrhea, reflecting multi-system involvement.
Diazinon induced reactive oxygen species generation and HO-1 expression at 150 µM without affecting cell viability in RBL-2H3 mast cells.
Diazinon inhibited A23187-mediated degranulation in RBL-2H3 mast cells without affecting calcium influx.

Diazinon suppressed Il4 gene expression induced by A23187 in RBL-2H3 mast cells.
